open_errors.issue: Devan never lies to Neela (bible voice note). On the terrace he tells her and Kannan he has to see Bhaskaran about the gate, and the narration confirms it was not true.
open_errors.fix: Give him a true excuse for walking away, and change the narration so it no longer calls the line a lie.

patches.find: He set the water pot on the wall. He said, "I have to see Bhaskaran about the gate," and walked down the terrace steps without looking back.
patches.replace: He set the water pot on the wall. He said, "I need a moment," and walked down the terrace steps without looking back.

patches.find: It was not true. The wall by the cistern was near enough that he could stand there, palm flat on the cold laterite, until the chain went and covered the sound of his own breathing.
patches.replace: It was true, and it was all he would say. The wall by the cistern was near enough that he could stand there, palm flat on the cold laterite, until the chain went and covered the sound of his own breathing.

open_errors.issue: Devan never lies to Neela. Asked why Raiu was sent from the passage, he answers "Oil.", and the narration has just said the order did not save oil.
open_errors.fix: Replace the false reason with a true one that reveals nothing, and adjust her reply to match.

patches.find: "Then I'll be sparing with mine," she said, and pinched out the wick.
patches.replace: "Then mine can keep it company," she said, and pinched out the wick.

open_errors.issue: Devan tells Neela "I'll be asleep" at dusk. In ch 15 he says he has been awake for every dusk turning she made in the room, so the statement was knowingly false.
open_errors.fix: Make his line literally true (in bed) and match her reply.

patches.replace: "Then I'll look at it in bed."

open_errors.issue: Devan tells Neela he didn't know his breath hitches. In his own POV (ch 2, ch 5) he knows his breath has a small hitch, and in ch 16 and 17 he produces it deliberately for her to count. This is a lie to Neela.
open_errors.fix: Have him say he didn't know she counted it, which is true at this point.

patches.find:
"I didn't know it did that."

"It does."
patches.replace:
"I didn't know you counted it."

"I do."

open_errors.issue: Freshly cut with blackbark gall and going numb, Devan tells Neela "I'm fine." He never lies to her.
open_errors.fix: Replace with a true short answer.

open_errors.issue: Devan tells Neela his shaking is 'the ribs', and she immediately says it isn't. A false reason given to her breaks his never-lies trait.
open_errors.fix: Have him give a partial truth and let her correct the rest.

patches.find: "It isn't." She kept her hand where it was. "I know where the ribs are."
patches.replace: "Not this part." She kept her hand where it was. "I know where the ribs are."

open_errors.issue: When not in use the shutter bar hangs on hooks on the wall (ch 1, ch 3), and the iron brackets hold it across the shutters. In ch 10, by day with the shutters open, the bar is said to lie along the wall on its two iron brackets.
open_errors.fix: Put the idle bar on its hooks.

patches.find: The bar lay along the wall on its two iron brackets, seasoned teak, thick as her forearm.
patches.replace: The bar lay along the wall on its two hooks, seasoned teak, thick as her forearm.

open_errors.issue: Bindu is Kannan's singing mother, known at the fort from ch 5. In ch 9 'Bindu, who sang' is listed among pass-village women whose names Neela learns for the first time on the road.
open_errors.fix: Give the village woman a different name.

patches.find: Bindu, who sang. A grandfather called Kesu with one eye.
patches.replace: Saroja, who sang at the well. A grandfather called Kesu with one eye.

open_errors.issue: Ammu's market cover is Valli, a coast-side pepper trader's girl (ch 7, ch 26, ch 28). In ch 18 she carries a tray of cheap bangles and is called a bangle seller.
open_errors.fix: Keep her in the pepper-trader cover.

patches.find: Her cover was a coast girl's blue cotton and a tray of cheap bangles, and under it she looked sharp as a split reed.
patches.replace: Her cover was a coast girl's blue cotton and a pepper trader's sack, and under it she looked sharp as a split reed.

patches.find: Then, light again, a bangle seller once more:
patches.replace: Then, light again, Valli the pepper girl once more:
